records.name: Complex Factory Hierarchies
records.definition: Building elaborate parallel factory class hierarchies where cloning an existing configured instance would suffice.

records.name: Concrete Constructor Coupling
records.definition: Instantiating concrete classes directly with constructors, coupling callers to specific implementations.

records.name: Global Mutable State
records.definition: Exposing global variables that any code can mutate, creating hidden coupling and nondeterminism.

records.name: Mixed Product Families
records.definition: Combining products from different incompatible families, producing inconsistent sets of objects.

records.name: Scattered Construction Logic
records.definition: Spreading object-creation logic across many call sites instead of centralizing it in a factory.

records.name: Telescoping Constructor
records.definition: Overloading constructors with ever more parameters to cover optional fields, producing unreadable call sites.

records.name: Controlled Instantiation
records.definition: The ability to govern how and when an object is created.

records.name: Deferred Instantiation
records.definition: The ability to let subclasses decide which class to instantiate, deferring the choice from the base class.

records.name: Dynamic Object Creation
records.definition: The ability to create new objects at runtime by cloning existing configured instances.

records.name: Family-Level Replacement
records.definition: The ability to swap an entire family of related products by changing a single factory.

records.name: Polymorphic Construction
records.definition: The ability to create objects through a common interface without naming their concrete classes.

records.name: Shared Resource Access
records.definition: The ability to give many callers coordinated access to one shared resource.

records.name: Valid Object Creation
records.definition: The ability to construct an object only once all its required parts are supplied and validated.

records.name: Cloneable Template Object
records.definition: The requirement that a prototype object support being copied to produce new instances.

records.name: Creation Variation
records.definition: A precondition that different variants of a product must be produced depending on runtime context.

records.name: Related Product Variants
records.definition: The requirement that products form families of related variants meant to be used together.

records.name: Single-Instance Need
records.definition: A precondition that exactly one instance of a type must exist across the system.

records.name: Subclass-Controlled Creation
records.definition: The requirement that subclasses determine which concrete product a creator instantiates.

records.name: Complex Construction
records.definition: The degree of complexity in assembling an object that motivates a step-by-step builder.

records.name: Copy Semantics
records.definition: The degree of care required to define correct deep versus shallow copying when cloning objects.

records.name: Inheritance Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which relying on subclassing to vary creation adds to the inheritance hierarchy's complexity.

records.name: Constructor-Valid State
records.definition: A technique for having a constructor or factory accept only arguments that produce a valid object.

records.name: Repeated Expensive Setup
records.definition: A defect in which each new object repeats a costly setup that copying a prepared instance would avoid.
